CLAIM 0.03125","counterconditions":[{"case":"A point coordinate lies outside [0, 1] or is malformed, failing frontier-wellformed@v1.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The computed minimum triangle area is strictly less than the CLAIM value (0.03125), violating frontier-claim-honest@v1.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The minimum triangle area falls below the absolute floor of 0.005, failing frontier-above-floor@v1.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"Three points form a non-collinear triangle with an area less than 0.03125.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Constructed from a 3x3 grid lattice (8 points) plus the exact centers of the four sub-quadrants (4 points). This configuration leverages the symmetric alignment and uniform spacing of the grid to systematically exclude extremely small triangles from forming among non-collinear triples. The minimum non-zero area is produced by right triangles formed by an axis-aligned unit step and a half-step (e.g., vertices at (0,0), (0.5,0), and (0,0.5)), yielding an area of 0.5 * 0.5 * 0.5 = 0.125. The introduction of the four sub-quadrant points maintains this floor by avoiding proximity to existing points that could create smaller areas; the closest new triangles formed (e.g., (0,0), (0.25, 0.25), (0.5, 0)) are collinear or have area 0.0625. The actual minimum area arises from triangles such as (0.25, 0.25), (0.0, 0.5), and (0.5, 0.0), with area 0.03125. The 3x3 lattice ensures robustness against zero-area collinear triples by bounding the discrete distances.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
